name: Balinese subak irrigation cooperation
summary: Bali's subak system, in which farmer groups jointly share and manage irrigation water through channels and weirs, with roots traced to the ninth century.
description: Cooperative Balinese irrigation management through farmer groups and a network of channels and weirs; present water-temple features are not individually dated to its earliest phase.
tier_reason: Retain my1 for a durable cooperative irrigation institution spanning communities/generations; an isolated graph node is not evidence of low importance. Practice fits. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.
why: Terraced rice farming on steep volcanic slopes required neighbours to share and schedule water from the same rivers and springs.

date.label: by c. 900 CE
date.basis: UNESCO describes the subak system as dating back to the ninth century; the bound is a broad historical estimate.

events.caveats: UNESCO’s broad summary does not date each existing temple, channel, rule or local group to the ninth century; this is not proof of uniform or uninterrupted institutions.
